trials.subject: Home garden · the greenhouse frame
trials.prompt: Create a single new landscape documentary photograph of this exact Cornish home garden during the greenhouse construction in March 2022. Use the reference as a location and build-stage photograph. Imagine the photographer stepped about one pace left on the lawn and lowered the camera to just above waist height, looking more squarely into the doorway gable while still seeing the near long side. Compose a landscape 3:2 medium-wide view with the whole ridge, base corner and door opening comfortably inside the frame. Keep the same modest building, footprint and height, fine unpainted aluminium extrusions, open pitched roof and slender bracing, narrow upright door aperture, timber-edged bed in near foreground and low grey brickwork with internal beds on either side of a central aisle. The perimeter plinth breaks at the door threshold. This is the erection stage: metal frame in place, glazing still to come, a short ladder laid loose inside. All joints and uprights make practical sense. The actual bright blue flat-roofed timber shed with small side windows sits beyond the left end, pale blue double gate farther left, weathered grey panel fence and sparse climbing stems along the back right; keep the landmarks and the tight suburban proportions in their original order. The view through the empty frame matters. Cool diffuse March daylight, ordinary raked soil, natural surface detail, a casual but clear eye for what a gardener needs to see. No people, drawing, collage, captions, watermarks, markings, extra greenhouse or invented outbuildings. Make an authentic new photograph from the specified viewpoint, not a copy of the reference.
trials.review: The new angle preserves the blue shed, gate, weathered fence and unglazed frame on a low masonry perimeter. The doorway framing and gable members warrant a technical check before use as an erection illustration. H09 shows a later glazed structure from a different position.

trials.subject: Allotment · the covered beds and shed
trials.prompt: Create a single new photorealistic 3:2 landscape documentary photograph on the specific Cornish allotment in the reference photographs. Camera on the grass path, turned slightly left across the edge of John's own beds at about chest height. Make it a plausible March afternoon at gardener's eye level. His small PALE MINT GREEN timber shed sits at the far end of his rows, slightly left of centre in the middle distance. Use the FIRST image A02 as the controlling map: John's ground is the left part reaching almost halfway across that aerial image and it ends just beyond the pale green shed. A thin strip of the shared grass path may enter at right. The brown shed belongs to the neighbouring plot to the right and may only be a small background glimpse. In the SECOND image A05, use the shed itself for its proportions, dark felt gable roof, mint bargeboards, plain vertically boarded door and horizontal sides. Most of the beds seen BEHIND it in that photo belong to another plot; do not transpose those beds into the camera foreground. The THIRD photograph is for credible ground-level scale, not its person or April activity. Subject of the new shot is the edge of a short planted bed with a section of fine off-white crop mesh held clear of the leaves over low simple supports and held down at the edges. Show some of the adjacent black covers weighted with spaced bricks, low rows of shoots, some bare soil, and worn grass matching John's actual plot in the first photo. Keep the shed identifiable and the actual suburban bungalow roofs and hedges discreetly beyond the allotments. Moderate depth of field so the texture of the mesh and the shed remain legible together. A matter-of-fact British gardening book photograph, soft daylight, natural colours, no people, graphics, lettering, collage or watermark. Do not turn the beds into a decorative enclosed garden.
trials.review: The pale green shed, grass path, covered rows and brick weights give a recognisable composition in the direction established by A02. The foreground mesh and planting are reconstructed. A03 looks back across the beds and cannot establish the exact position of individual plants or this camera.
